edges.description: The enzyme cannot turn over without its cofactor, despite being present and catalytically competent.
The conversion of dopamine to noradrenaline does not occur.
Only the noradrenergic arm of the autonomic nervous system loses its transmitter.

Adrenaline is a principal counter-regulatory hormone for falling blood glucose, so a disease that abolishes it removes that defence. This is a second downstream arm of the same lesion, not a coincidental finding.
Without noradrenergic vasoconstriction, standing produces an uncompensated fall in blood pressure.
The clinical manifestation of the lost counter-regulatory response.
Six knockout mice showed the catecholamine deficit in both brain and adrenal gland, which the authors describe as recapitulating the clinical phenotype.
edges.limitations: Mice, unlike humans, synthesize ascorbate de novo, so a mouse retains a source of the cofactor a patient does not have. For a disease defined by failure to recycle ascorbate, that is the strongest reason to expect the knockout to under-represent human severity, and it is why fidelity here is MODERATE rather than HIGH. Beyond that, the reported measurements are tissue catecholamine concentrations rather than haemodynamic phenotyping, so the model is shown to reproduce the biochemistry rather than the orthostatic hypotension itself; and the cohort is six animals.

edges.description: Absent noradrenaline with preserved dopamine reports a block at the dopamine-to-noradrenaline step specifically.
Read as a present-or-absent discriminator rather than as a magnitude: enzyme activity is present and normal while its product is absent, which establishes that the enzyme is not the lesion.

nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous CYB561 variants. Reported alleles include a missense change, a nonsense change and a whole-exon deletion, across two families and one further compound heterozygote.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in CYB561 Causing a Novel Orthostatic Hypotension Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Homozygosity mapping and exome and Sanger sequencing revealed pathogenic homozygous mutations in the gene encoding cytochrome b561 (CYB561); a missense variant c.262G>A, p.Gly88Arg in exon 3 in the Dutch family and a nonsense mutation (c.131G>A, p.Trp44*) in exon 2 in the American family.

nodes.description: Reproduces the central biochemical lesion, with reduced noradrenaline and normetanephrine in brain and reduced normetanephrine and metanephrine in adrenal tissue.

A synthetic noradrenaline precursor that is decarboxylated directly to noradrenaline by aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase, so it does not require dopamine beta-hydroxylase or its cofactor. It therefore bypasses the entire lesion rather than correcting it.

Dopamine beta-hydroxylase activity fails in situ while measured plasma enzyme activity is normal and the DBH gene is intact. This dissociation is the single most useful diagnostic feature and the reason the disease is a phenocopy rather than a variant of DBH deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in CYB561 Causing a Novel Orthostatic Hypotension Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Plasma dopamine β-hydroxylase activity, however, was normal, and the DBH gene had no mutations.

nodes.description: Without adrenaline, the counter-regulatory response to falling glucose is lost, and patients experience recurrent symptomatic hypoglycaemia from infancy. In one reported patient it was severe enough to prompt a partial pancreatectomy at age three - which did not help, since the defect is in the counter-regulation rather than in insulin secretion.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in CYB561 Causing a Novel Orthostatic Hypotension Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: DβH and CYB561 deficiency are both characterized by orthostatic hypotension, recurrent hypoglycemia and low norepinephrine levels.

nodes.description: Ascorbate inside the catecholamine secretory vesicle is consumed and not replaced. This is the specific compartmental shortage that defines the disease.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in CYB561 Causing a Novel Orthostatic Hypotension Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The CYB561 protein defect leads to a shortage of ascorbate inside the catecholamine secretory vesicles leading to a functional dopamine β-hydroxylase deficiency.

nodes.description: Cytochrome b561 carries electrons from cytosolic ascorbate across the vesicle membrane using two haem-b centres, one on each face. That transfer is what regenerates ascorbate inside the vesicle, a compartment the cell cannot simply refill from outside.
nodes.id: Loss of Transmembrane Electron Transfer into Secretory Vesicles

evidence.reference_title: Spectral and Redox Properties of a Recombinant Mouse Cytochrome b561 Protein Suggest Transmembrane Electron Transfer Function.
evidence.snippet: The major characteristics of these proteins are their ascorbate reducibility and trans-membrane electron transferring capability.

nodes.description: Noradrenaline and its metabolites are undetectable while dopamine and its metabolites are normal - the biochemical signature of a block at exactly this step.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital absence of norepinephrine due to CYB561 mutations.
evidence.snippet: Plasma norepinephrine and metabolites were undetectable, and plasma dopamine and metabolites were normal.

nodes.description: Lifelong, disabling, and the presenting problem in every reported patient.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital absence of norepinephrine due to CYB561 mutations.
evidence.snippet: Patients had disabling lifelong orthostatic hypotension (OH) and impaired blood pressure response to the Valsalva maneuver (VM), with exaggerated hypotension during phase 2 and lack of overshoot during phase 4.

evidence.snippet: Patient A1 underwent a partial pancreatectomy at age three years for this reason but she showed no improvement in these episodes.

nodes.description: Sympathetic noradrenergic function fails while sympathetic cholinergic function (sweating) and parasympathetic function (heart rate regulation) remain normal. The selectivity follows directly from which transmitter the missing cofactor serves.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital absence of norepinephrine due to CYB561 mutations.
evidence.snippet: CYB561 deficiency is characterized by selective sympathetic noradrenergic failure with lifelong, disabling OH but with normal sympathetic cholinergic (sweating) and parasympathetic (heart rate regulation) functions.
